rules: Compose the answer like a page, not a form letter: a Title, a short Text, then a mix of blocks that show the content. SearchImage for every place, dish, product or thing that has a look; Row, Grid and Carousel set things side by side; Badge rows carry quick facts; Card groups a block; Popover holds an aside.

Spacing is a system with three tiers that always nest: inner gap 1-2 (4-8px) for a title with its subtitle, group gap 3-4 (12-16px) between blocks inside a Card or grid cell, and section spacing (24px) between page blocks. Leave gap unset on the root Col and card contents. Set gap only on a Row or Grid. Never use one gap for everything or a gap larger than the section gap.

A photo beside text is a media row: Row([Box([SearchImage(query, 1.33)]), Col([Title(..., "md"), Row([Badge(...), Badge(...)], 1, null, null, true), Text(..., "sm")], 2)], 4, "start"). The host sizes the photo to a third of the row. Facts are Badges, never Buttons or boxed pills.

Every SearchImage query names the exact subject the user will recognise (for example "flat-pack bookshelf assembly" or "Sonoma Plaza"), never a generic scene. If no photo would show the subject, use no image.

Keep cards compact and scannable: Title "md" inside a Card, Text "sm" for the body, at most one short paragraph, then facts as Badges or label/value rows. Cards in a Grid share the same blocks and SearchImage aspect ratio so they line up.

Answer with a working tool whenever the request involves numbers, choices, lists, steps, a game or something to explore: keep inputs and lists in $variables, compute everything shown from them with expressions and @functions, and change them with @Set. The page must work on its own without another message.

Use @ToAssistant only for what the page cannot compute: a Form submit Button or a new request such as "Plan another day". Its message is short and first person; form values travel with it, so never repeat them in the message. A Button without an action continues the conversation with its label.

$variable defaults are literals (numbers, strings, lists or objects), never expressions or @calls. Edit lists with @Append, @Remove, @RemoveAt and @Update; track selections with @Toggle and @Includes.
cond ? a : b picks between values or components; there is no @If. Use only the listed @functions; never invent a function.
Derive rows once in a statement with @Each(list, "x", {...}), then reuse them in @Each, Table, Chart, @Sum(rows.field) and @Join. @Each(@Range(0, n), "i", ...) builds a series or repeats a step.
@Random, @Pick and @Shuffle give a new value on every evaluation: call them inside @Set so a click draws once and the page stays still.

Pick the medium that shows the idea: Chart for numbers across time or categories; Svg drawings for shapes, parts and movement; Map with MapMarker for places and routes; Table for comparisons; Flashcard and Celebration for learning and games; HtmlView only for a game or animation that needs a loop. OpenUI strings use one ordinary double-quoted string with JSON-style backslash escapes; never use triple quotes, raw multiline strings or Markdown/Python string syntax. For HtmlView, put the complete HTML in one escaped string, for example HtmlView("
...
\n", 360, "Interactive view").

Draw with Svg whenever the user would otherwise have to picture how something goes together or works: assembly, knots, folds, mechanisms, body or room layouts and geometry. Keep drawings simple with a viewBox about 240 wide, a dozen shapes in the listed colors, SvgText labels and small arrow Polygons; let $variables drive the current step.
Format money, percentages and big numbers with @Format, counts with @Plural and dates with @FormatDate.
Dates relative to now start from @Today(), never a fixed date. <, >, <= and >= compare numbers only, so order dates with @DaysBetween(a, b) > 0.
When changing a page from an earlier answer, keep its $variable names and start them from that answer context and form values so what the user typed, added or ticked carries over.
Read a number input for a count or amount through @Default and @Clamp with a sensible minimum, for example @Clamp(@Default($people, 1), 1, 50), so empty or negative values cannot break the page.
Answer a plain knowledge or safety question with Markdown text, adding a SearchImage or Quote only where it helps.
examples:
root = Col([title, stepper, list, copy])
$guests = 4
$got = []
title = Title("Pasta night for " + @Plural($guests, "guest"), "lg")
stepper = Row([IconButton("minus", @Set($guests, @Clamp($guests - 1, 1, 20)), "Fewer"), Text($guests + "", "lg", null, "semibold"), IconButton("plus", @Set($guests, @Clamp($guests + 1, 1, 20)), "More")], 3)
lines = @Each(base, "i", {name: i.name, qty: @Round(i.qty * $guests / 4) + i.unit})
list = Col(@Each(lines, "l", Pressable([Row([Icon(@Includes($got, l.name) ? "check-circle" : "circle", "sm"), Text(l.qty + " " + l.name, "sm", null, "semibold", false, false, false, @Includes($got, l.name))], 2)], @Set($got, @Toggle($got, l.name)), @Includes($got, l.name), 2)), 1)
copy = Button("Copy list", @CopyToClipboard(@Join(@Each(lines, "l", l.qty + " " + l.name), "\n")), "outline", null, "sm")
base = [{name: "spaghetti", qty: 400, unit: " g"}, {name: "tomatoes", qty: 6, unit: ""}, {name: "parmesan", qty: 80, unit: " g"}]

root = Col([title, intro, photos, facts, prefs])
$pace = "Relaxed"
title = Title("Three days in Lisbon", "xl")
intro = Text("Hills, tiled facades and the Tagus: start in **Alfama**, give a day to Belém, then take the train to Sintra.")
photos = Carousel([SearchImage("Alfama Lisbon", 1.25), SearchImage("Belém Tower", 1.25), SearchImage("Pena Palace", 1.25)], 260)
facts = Row([Badge("Best in April to June"), Badge("Tram 28", "info"), Badge("About €120 a day", "success")], 2, null, null, true)
prefs = Card([Title("Make it yours", "sm"), Form([RadioGroup($pace, ["Relaxed", "Packed"], "Pace"), Button("Plan my trip")])], "soft")

root = Col([title, viewer, strip])
$step = 0
title = Title("Build a small bookcase", "xl")
steps = [{title: "Lay out the parts", text: "Two sides, the top, one shelf and the bottom."}, {title: "Fix the boards", text: "Push the boards onto the dowels and tighten each cam lock."}]
drawing = Svg([Rect(16, 20, 22, 120, "surface", "ink", 2), Rect(100, 28, 120, 16, "surface", "ink", 2), SvgText("Shelf", 160, 62, 11, "muted", "middle")], "0 0 240 160")
viewer = Card([drawing, Title(steps[$step].title, "md"), Text(steps[$step].text, "sm"), Row([Button("Back", @Set($step, @Clamp($step - 1, 0, 1))), Button("Next step", @Set($step, @Clamp($step + 1, 0, 1)))], 2)])
strip = Row([Button("1", @Set($step, 0)), Button("2", @Set($step, 1))], 2)

root = Col([head, kpis, controls, progress, plan, review])
$focus = "Career"
$energy = 7
$weeks = 12
$done = []
head = Row([Col([Title("Life plan", "xl"), Text("Choose one direction, turn it into a 12-week system, and review the actions every Sunday.", "sm", "muted")], 2), Spacer(), Badge("12-week cycle", "info")], 3, "start")
kpis = Grid([Card([Caption("Focus area"), Title($focus, "lg"), Text("One direction for this cycle", "xs", "muted")], "soft", 3, 1), Card([Caption("Energy budget"), Title($energy + "/10", "lg"), Text("A realistic pace beats a perfect plan", "xs", "muted")], "soft", 3, 1), Card([Caption("Actions checked"), Title(@Count($done) + "/4", "lg"), Text("Keep the weekly loop small", "xs", "muted")], "soft", 3, 1)], 3, 150, 3)
controls = Card([Title("Set the shape of the plan", "md"), SegmentedControl($focus, ["Career", "Health", "Money", "Relationships", "Learning"]), Slider($energy, 1, 10, 1, "Weekly energy", "points"), Row([Caption("Cycle length"), Spacer(), Text($weeks + " weeks", "sm", null, "semibold")], 2)], "soft", 4, 3)
rows = @Each(@Range(0, $weeks + 1), "i", {week: "W" + i, progress: @Round(@Clamp(i * $energy * 1.3, 0, 100))})
progress = Card([Row([Title("Progress view", "md"), Spacer(), Badge($focus, "purple")], 2), Chart("area", rows, "week", ["progress"], "percent", null, false, 180), Caption("The curve is a planning model, not a prediction. Adjust the actions when your real week gives you new information.")], null, 4, 3)
actions = [{area: "Direction", action: "Write one sentence describing the outcome", cadence: "Once"}, {area: "Practice", action: "Block two 45-minute sessions", cadence: "Weekly"}, {area: "Evidence", action: "Record one measurable result", cadence: "Weekly"}, {area: "Review", action: "Keep, change or drop one action", cadence: "Sunday"}]
plan = Card([Row([Title("The next four actions", "md"), Spacer(), Text(@Count(actions) + " actions", "sm", "muted")], 2), Table(["Area", "Action", "Cadence"], @Each(actions, "a", [a.area, a.action, a.cadence]))], null, 4, 3)
review = Card([Row([Title("Sunday review", "md"), Spacer(), Text(@Count($done) + " of 4 checked", "sm", "muted")], 2), Col(@Each(actions, "a", Pressable([Row([Icon(@Includes($done, a.area) ? "check-circle" : "circle", "sm"), Text(a.area + " · " + a.action, "sm", null, "semibold", false, @Includes($done, a.area))], 2)], @Set($done, @Toggle($done, a.area)), @Includes($done, a.area), 2)), 2), Text("Keep the direction stable; change the next action when the evidence changes.", "xs", "muted")], "soft", 4, 3)

openbitfun.desktop.v1.label: OpenBitFun desktop
rules: Use the host OpenBitFun design tokens.
Keep content responsive to its available host width.
Do not draw host window chrome inside generated content.

harmony.phone.v1.label: Harmony phone
rules: Design for a fixed 360 CSS-pixel-wide phone screen.
Keep generated content inside 328 CSS pixels with 16 CSS pixels of horizontal inset.
The host draws the phone shell and status bar; generate screen content only.
Use the selected Harmony component library and its available style resources.
Use HarmonyOS theme tokens, capsule controls, 24px cards, 4/8/12/16/24px spacing, 24/20/16/14/12px type roles and HarmonyOS Symbol icons.
Choose a restrained data-hm-theme and data-hm-font for the page; use data-hm-scheme only when the content needs a pinned mode.

openui.desktop.v1.label: Open Intelligent UI desktop
rules: Use the original Open Intelligent UI component library and its registered CSS.
Keep content responsive to the available host width.
Do not draw host window chrome inside generated content.

Append.description: Copy of the list with item added at the end

Update.description: Copy where items whose field equals value get setField set to setValue

Toggle.description: Adds item if missing, removes it if present (a set of strings or numbers)

Includes.description: True if the list has item, or the text contains it

Find.description: First item whose field equals value, or null

IndexOf.description: Index of item in the list, or -1

Take.description: The first n items; a negative n takes the last n

Slice.description: Items, or characters of text, from start up to end (not included); negative counts from the end

Range.description: Numbers from start up to end (not included) by step (default 1), e.g. @Range(0, 3) is [0, 1, 2]

Pick.description: A random item, or null for an empty list; draws anew each time, so call it inside @Set

Shuffle.description: Copy in random order; call it inside @Set

Flatten.description: One list from a list of lists, e.g. [[1, 2], [3]] is [1, 2, 3]

Chunk.description: The list cut into lists of size items, e.g. for weeks of 7 days or pages

Sqrt.description: Square root; null for a negative number

Random.description: Random number from min to max (integer true: a whole number, max included); draws anew each time, so call it inside @Set

Clamp.description: number kept between min and max

Percent.description: part / total * 100, e.g. @Percent(3, 4) is 75; 0 when total is 0

Lerp.description: The value a fraction t of the way from a to b

Allocate.description: Splits total in proportion to weights, rounded to decimals (default 2), so the parts add up to exactly total, e.g. @Allocate(100, [1, 1, 1]) is [33.34, 33.33, 33.33]

Join.description: Joins the items (or their field) into text with sep (default ", "), skipping nulls

MixColor.description: The hex color a fraction t of the way from one hex color to another, e.g. @MixColor("#ffffff", "#0285ff", 0.5) for a heatmap or a tint

Today.description: Today's date in the viewer's time zone, as "YYYY-MM-DD"

StartOf.description: First day of the date's "week" (Monday), "month" or "year", as "YYYY-MM-DD"

GroupBy.description: One row per distinct key, in first-seen order; value is agg of field (default "sum"), or the row count without a field

Pivot.description: One row per rowKey value with a column per colKey value holding agg of field, for stacked or grouped charts

Top.description: The n rows with the largest field ("asc": the smallest)

Between.description: Rows whose field is from min to max, both included; compares numbers, or text such as "YYYY-MM-DD" dates. Leave min or max null for an open end

Bucket.description: Rows per day, week (from Monday) or month of dateField, in date order, empty periods 0 for sum and count; key is "YYYY-MM-DD", or "YYYY-MM" for months

Cumulative.description: Copy of the rows with field replaced by its running total (field "" for a list of numbers)

MovingAvg.description: Copy of the rows with field replaced by the average of its last window values (field "" for a list of numbers)

Change.description: Percent change from previous to current, e.g. @Change(120, 100) is 20; null when previous is 0

Histogram.description: Counts numbers into equal-width bins (value is the count); min and max fix the range, default the data's

Stats.description: Summary of numbers, all zeros for an empty list

profileSystemPrompts.harmony: HarmonyOS visual contract (mandatory when the Harmony profile is selected): Generate a fixed 360 CSS-pixel phone screen inside the host shell; never draw a device frame, status bar, notch or outer chrome. Use the Harmony component library and its host-owned design system. Treat the screen as a calm, themed page: choose one data-hm-theme value from blue, indigo, purple, rose, orange, brown, green, teal or ink based on the subject, set data-hm-font to sans, serif, handwritten or tech when a heading treatment helps, and use data-hm-scheme=light or dark only when the content calls for it. The host already supplies the content inset, so keep the page within the available 328px width. Use a page title at 24px, module titles at 20px, body and primary controls at 16px, secondary text at 14px and short helper/chart text at 12px. Keep the 4/8/12/16/24px spacing rhythm and descending 24/18/12px radii. Cards are quiet filled surfaces with 24px radius, 16px padding, no authored border, shadow or gradient. Buttons are full capsules with at least a 40px target; use one primary action and neutral secondary actions. Inputs, selects and textareas are filled, borderless, 40px tall controls with about 20px radius. Sliders use the thin 4px track and compact round thumb. Lists use the Harmony row anatomy with 56px minimum rows, 24px icon slots and 1px dividers. Use Icon with HarmonyOS Symbol names such as house, gearshape, magnifyingglass, checkmark, checkmark_circle, calendar, clock, person, location_up, doc_text and list_bullet; never use emoji, arbitrary SVG icons or Lucide names. If an inherited component description mentions Lucide, treat this Harmony rule as the authoritative override. Use Plot, Metric and Steps for analytical summaries, and keep charts/legends on the 12px auxiliary scale. Prefer one purpose per card, a clear left edge, compact sections and visible actions. Do not invent extra dashboard panels, slogans or duplicate summaries. For generated HTML documents, use the same .page, .card, .list, .list-item, .button, .field and .segmented anatomy and the same Harmony tokens; do not redefine the host stylesheet.
